42912667.text: Urethral involvement in IgG4-related disease is rare. We describe FDG PET/CT and delayed pelvic PET/MRI findings in a woman with IgG4-related disease presenting as urethral wall thickening with obstructive urinary symptoms. FDG PET/CT and delayed pelvic PET/MRI showed significant circumferential thickening of the urethral wall with intense diffuse activity (SUV max , 13) and multiple hypermetabolic lymph nodes in pelvic, retroperitoneal, mediastinal, pulmonary hilar, and axillary regions. This case indicates that IgG4-related urethral disease should be included in the differential diagnosis of FDG-avid urethral or periurethral lesions.

42951717.text: Bone metastases are a major cause of pain, skeletal complications, marrow compromise and mortality in advanced prostate cancer. The therapeutic biology of skeletal disease is heterogeneous: malignant epithelial cells expressing prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) coexist with osteoblasts, osteoclasts, reactive mineralising bone and variable marrow infiltration. Radium-223 dichloride is a bone-seeking alpha emitter with randomised evidence of overall-survival benefit in selected men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), whereas PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy delivers radiation to PSMA-expressing tumour deposits in bone and soft tissues. Their mechanistic complementarity has motivated sequential and concurrent strategies, but complementary localisation does not itself establish clinical synergy. This review critically integrates ALSYMPCA, ERA-223, PEACE-3, VISION, TheraP, PSMAfore, RALU and AlphaBet, together with radiobiology, molecular imaging, marrow and skeletal toxicity, dosimetry and evolving therapeutic sequencing. The final 133-patient retrospective RALU report describes the safety and outcomes observed after radium-223 followed by lutetium-177-PSMA in selected heavily pretreated patients; AlphaBet reports preliminary safety and antitumour activity with concurrent lutetium-177-PSMA-I&T and radium-223 in a single-arm early-phase study. Neither provides randomised evidence of an incremental survival benefit for dual-radionuclide treatment. Conversely, PEACE-3 establishes an overall-survival benefit for radium-223 combined with enzalutamide under contemporary bone-protective practice, whereas ERA-223 underscores the fracture hazards of inappropriate combinations. Future trials must integrate lesion-level imaging, whole-body disease phenotype, marrow reserve, patient-reported outcomes, competing systemic treatments and personalised radiation exposure. The most defensible clinical strategy is evidence-weighted selection of radionuclide therapy according to disease distribution and treatment history, with concurrent dual-radionuclide approaches restricted to appropriately governed trials.

42988567.text: With a prevalence above 10% worldwide, chronic kidney disease is one of the leading medical burdens. Independent of the underlying cause, kidney fibrosis emerges as the common final endpoint and serves as the most robust predictor of disease progression and long-term prognosis. Fibrosis is driven by extracellular matrix-producing mesenchymal cells, which are characterized by platelet-derived growth factor receptor β (PDGFRβ) expression. PDGFRβ also mediates fibrogenesis in these cells and represents a potential therapeutic target for direct intervention or a potential anchor for selective delivery of antifibrotic drugs. Diagnostic approaches assessing PDGFRβ expression in kidneys are missing. Here, we developed and evaluated a novel tracer using a PDGFRβ-targeting biparatopic variable domain of a heavy-chain-only antibody construct, designated SP02SP26-ABD, for in vivo, noninvasive, molecular imaging of kidney fibrosis. Methods: PDGFRβ expression was assessed in human kidney biopsies and publicly available transcriptomic datasets. In vivo imaging studies were performed in 2 distinct murine models of kidney fibrosis using fluorescence imaging and 89Zr-labeled PET. Specificity and dose dependency were evaluated using a nonspecific control variable domain of a heavy-chain-only antibody construct, R2R2-ABD, and coinjection of increasing amounts of unlabeled SP02SP26-ABD. Ex vivo biodistribution and correlation with histologic and molecular markers of fibrosis were performed. Results: PDGFRβ was increased in fibrotic human kidneys across multiple disease entities, predominantly localized to pericytes and fibroblasts, supporting its relevance as a translational imaging target. In vivo imaging demonstrated significantly higher tracer accumulation in fibrotic compared with nonfibrotic kidneys across both models, whereas tracer accumulation in nonrenal organs was low, with minimal uptake in the spleen. We found no difference between fibrotic and nonfibrotic kidneys when using a nonspecific R2R2-ABD control construct, whereas increasing amounts of unlabeled SP02SP26-ABD led to a dose-dependent decrease in tracer accumulation, consistent with a saturation effect. Tracer signal correlated with PDGFRβ expression, confirming the specificity of the approach. Conclusion: We provide the first proof of concept for noninvasive PET imaging of PDGFRβ-expressing fibrogenic cells in kidney disease, supporting further development of this approach for specific, noninvasive assessment of kidney fibrosis.

43002567.text: We present a patient with biochemical recurrence after salvage radiation and combined androgen deprivation therapy with abiraterone who underwent 18F-PSMA PET/CT for a rapidly rising prostate-specific antigen (PSA). The scan revealed an intense prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-avid focus in the cecum without an apparent CT correlate. Colonoscopy identified a smooth, 2 cm nonobstructing cecal mass, and biopsy confirmed metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma by morphology and immunohistochemistry. This case demonstrates 18F-PSMA PET/CT detection at a low PSA level of a clinically occult metastatic lesion involving the cecum, an exceptionally rare site for prostate cancer spread. Colonoscopy and biopsy confirmation of atypical PSMA-avid gastrointestinal lesions remain essential, as physiologic colonic uptake, PSMA-avid diverticula, and PSMA-expressing primary colorectal cancers are well-documented mimickers.

43020617.text: [177Lu]Lu-PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy is delivered as repeated cycles, yet the decision to continue or adapt treatment after the second cycle is not standardized. Posttherapy SPECT/CT is routinely performed but rarely used formally for response assessment. We developed a multimodality, response-adapted algorithm applied after cycle 2 and tested its concordance with real-world decisions. Methods: We studied 142 men with metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant prostate cancer (formerly metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer) who completed at least 2 cycles of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA and underwent posttherapy SPECT/CT, baseline and 12-wk prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing, and baseline and interim prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET and [18F]FDG PET. Response was assessed in accordance with Prostate Cancer Working Group 4 recommendations for PSA and with RECIP 1.0 for SPECT and PSMA PET. The algorithm combined SPECT/CT and PSA, used PSMA PET only when both were stable, and yielded 3 recommendations: continue [177Lu]Lu-PSMA, discontinue [177Lu]Lu-PSMA, or consider [18F]FDG PET. The primary endpoints were the number of interim PSMA PET studies avoided and the concordance between algorithm recommendations (continue vs. discontinue) and real-world decisions. The secondary endpoint was intermodality response evaluation concordance. Results: The algorithm recommended continuation in 74 patients (52.1%), discontinuation in 49 patients (34.5%), and [18F]FDG PET in 19 patients (13.4%). Interim PSMA PET/CT could be avoided in 120 patients (84.5%) (95% CI, 77.7%-89.5%). Among patients with a definitive recommendation, conditional agreement of the algorithm with real-world management decisions was 91.1% (95% CI, 84.7%-94.9%), with a κ of 0.81 (95% CI, 0.69-0.91). All 74 patients (100%) with an algorithm recommendation to continue treatment had matching real-world decisions for treatment continuation, whereas 38 (78%) of 49 patients with an algorithm recommendation to discontinue treatment had matching real-world decisions for treatment discontinuation. Response classification on SPECT agreed only moderately with PSA level (κ = 0.45) and PSMA PET (κ = 0.47), but the combination of SPECT and PSA raised agreement with PSMA PET to "substantial" (κ = 0.67), approaching that of PSMA PET with PSA level (κ = 0.70). Every discordant decision (n = 11) occurred when the algorithm recommended treatment discontinuation in a patient who nonetheless continued treatment, most commonly because [177Lu]Lu-PSMA was being used as a last line of therapy (7/11, 64%). Conclusion: A SPECT-guided algorithm could have avoided most interim PSMA PET studies and reproduced real-world treatment decisions after 2 cycles of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA with high agreement. This algorithm may serve as the basis for a standardized treatment management framework, pending independent, prospective outcome-based validation.

43043467.text: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound Liver Imaging Reporting and Data System (CEUS LI-RADS) version 2017 provides a standardized framework for characterizing focal liver observations in patients at high risk for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Although the system has demonstrated clinical utility and is endorsed by the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases, accumulating validation evidence reveals an existing gap that limits the application of CEUS LI‑RADS to liver observations beyond those categorized as CEUS LR‑5 for HCC. This limitation arises mainly from the specificity‑prioritized design of CEUS LR‑5 for HCC, which comes at the cost of sensitivity. In this review, we summarize a group of studies on CEUS LI‑RADS for liver observations, addressing their merits, limitations, and proposals for revision. The proposed modifications are investigational, and have not been incorporated into current guidelines. Our objectives are to reduce misclassification, improve the sensitivity of CEUS LR-5 for HCC while maintaining reasonably high specificity, expand the utility of CEUS LI-RADS to a broader range of liver observations, and ultimately optimize patient management. The 60-s threshold for early washout onset lacks statistical derivation and leads to substantial misclassification of HCC as LR-M (probably or definitely malignant, not necessarily HCC); reported HCC proportions among LR-M lesions range from 41.8% to 86.7%. The definitions of washout degrees (mild vs. marked) are somewhat ambiguous, which cause inter-reader variability, and the absence of objective quantitative metrics. Current discussions regarding potential modification of CEUS LI-RADS v2017 include: (1) shortening the early washout threshold from 60 to < 45 s or other threshold, which markedly improves sensitivity of CEUS LR 5 for HCC with minimal loss of specificity; (2) redefining marked washout as occurring at 3 min or later as an adjunctive criterion; (3) incorporating Kupffer-phase findings when using perfluorobutane (Sonazoid); (4) integrating ancillary features; and (5) considering size-stratified thresholds.

43076917.label: Objective
43076917.text: To assess the utility of excess parenchymal water (EPW) partial volume, quantified from multi-dynamic multi-echo (MDME)-based relaxometry, in distinguishing brain tumors.

43076917.label: Materials and methods
43076917.text: This retrospective study included 95 patients (61 with grade 4 adult-type diffuse gliomas, 16 with primary CNS lymphomas (PCNSLs), and 18 with brain metastases) who underwent preoperative MRI including MDME-based sequences between October 2022 and May 2025. EPW partial volume maps were generated using dedicated software. Peritumoral T2 hyperintense regions of interest (ROIs) were defined by subtracting manually drawn ROIs of the enhancing tumor on contrast-enhanced T1-weighted images from the whole T2 hyperintense areas. EPW partial volumes were compared among groups using the Kruskal-Wallis test with post hoc Dunn's tests and Bonferroni correction. Diagnostic performance was assessed by ROC curve analysis.

43076917.label: Results
43076917.text: The average EPW partial volume in the peritumoral T2 hyperintense area was significantly lower in grade 4 adult-type diffuse gliomas (median [IQR], 23.2% [14.6-30.5]) than in brain metastases (30.5% [21.7-37.3]) (p = 0.02). However, no significant differences in EPW partial volumes were observed between gliomas and PCNSLs (p = 0.85), or between PCNSLs and metastases (p = 0.65). The AUC was 0.71 (95% CI, 0.56-0.84) for differentiating gliomas from metastases. Using an EPW cutoff of 27.7%, the sensitivity and specificity were 67% and 71%, respectively.

43076917.label: Conclusion
43076917.text: EPW partial volume from MDME-based relaxometry was significantly lower in peritumoral areas of grade 4 adult-type diffuse gliomas than in brain metastases, suggesting its potential as a complementary quantitative biomarker for their differentiation.

43076917.label: Key points
43076917.text: Question Can excess parenchymal water partial volume derived from relaxometry distinguish different types of brain tumors? Findings In this pilot cohort, excess parenchymal water partial volume within peritumoral T2 hyperintense areas was significantly lower in grade 4 adult-type diffuse gliomas than in brain metastases, despite the modest diagnostic performance. Clinical relevance The average excess parenchymal water partial volume in the peritumoral T2 hyperintense area may complement conventional MRI by providing a quantitative measure that helps differentiate grade 4 adult-type diffuse gliomas from brain metastases.

43076967.label: Objective
43076967.text: To develop and temporally validate a bedside risk score (BTCH-AOMI) based exclusively on pre-CTA clinical variables to predict acute occlusive mesenteric ischemia (AOMI) in emergency CTA-selected patients.

43076967.label: Methods
43076967.text: We retrospectively evaluated 285 adult patients (development cohort [2017-2022]: n = 187, 85 AOMI; temporal validation cohort [2023-2024]: n = 98, 42 AOMI). A 0-5-point score was constructed using four pre-CTA predictors: abdominal distension (1 point), AOMI risk conditions (1 point), peritonitis (2 points), and bedside inflammatory response (1 point). Score performance was evaluated and compared with an operationalized "pain-out-of-proportion" rule.

43076967.label: Results
43076967.text: In temporal validation, the BTCH-AOMI score achieved moderate discrimination (AUC: 0.744, 95% CI: 0.651-0.834), significantly outperforming the pain-out-of-proportion rule (AUC: 0.521, 95% CI: 0.441-0.601; P = 0.002). Observed AOMI rates across validation strata (0-1, 2-3, and 4-5 points) were 25.0%, 45.5%, and 88.2%, respectively. A threshold of ≥ 2 points yielded a sensitivity of 71.4% and specificity of 64.3%; a threshold of ≥ 1 point yielded 95.2% sensitivity and 23.2% specificity.

43076967.label: Conclusions
43076967.text: The BTCH-AOMI score demonstrates moderate temporal discrimination and superior performance over traditional "pain-out-of-proportion" assessment. It is intended strictly as an adjunct for risk stratification and prioritization within emergency CTA pathways, not as a tool to exclude AOMI or replace CTA imaging.
